methodology: Public official APIs only. All derived values are computed from the series listed in this file.

series.label: GDP growth (annual %)
series.definition: Annual percentage change of real Gross Domestic Product at constant prices.
series.guide: Use it as the headline speed of the economy. Compare with inflation to see whether growth is real or price-driven.

series.label: GDP per capita (current US$)
series.definition: GDP divided by mid-year population, converted to current US dollars.
series.guide: A rough measure of average material output per person. It is not a measure of household income or welfare.

series.label: GDP per capita growth (annual %)
series.definition: Annual growth of real GDP divided by population growth.
series.guide: Prefer this over headline GDP growth when assessing whether average living standards are improving.

series.label: Consumer price inflation
series.definition: Annual percentage change in the Consumer Price Index.
series.guide: The rate at which a representative basket of consumer goods becomes more expensive. Compare with your own spending mix using the inflation tool.

series.label: Total population
series.definition: Mid-year estimate of the resident population.
series.guide: Denominator for per-capita metrics. Census 2011 below is the official decadal benchmark; this series is an annual estimate.

series.label: Population growth (annual %)
series.definition: Annual percentage change in population.
series.guide: Subtract this from GDP growth to approximate per-capita growth.

series.label: Urban population (% of total)
series.definition: Share of the population living in urban areas as defined by national statistical offices.
series.guide: A rising share usually signals structural change; pair it with productivity and housing data before drawing conclusions.

series.label: Working-age population (15–64, %)
series.definition: Share of the population aged 15 to 64 years.
series.guide: A demographic dividend exists only when this large cohort is employed and productive.

series.label: Life expectancy at birth
series.definition: Number of years a newborn would live if prevailing mortality patterns remained constant.
series.guide: A broad outcome measure for health, sanitation and nutrition. Moves slowly, so read multi-year trends.

series.label: Literacy rate (ages 15+)
series.definition: Percentage of people aged 15 and above who can read and write.
series.guide: Compare with the Census 2011 literacy benchmark below to gauge long-run educational progress.

series.label: Gross domestic savings (% of GDP)
series.definition: GDP minus final consumption expenditure, as a share of GDP.
series.guide: Higher savings give an economy more internally funded investment capacity.

series.label: Domestic credit to private sector (% of GDP)
series.definition: Financial resources provided to the private sector by banks and other financial corporations.
series.guide: A proxy for financial depth. Very rapid growth can also signal credit stress, so read it alongside savings.

series.label: Real interest rate
series.definition: Lending interest rate adjusted for inflation.
series.guide: Positive rates reward savers; deeply negative rates erode deposits. It is a market-wide rate, not your FD rate.

series.label: FDI inflows (% of GDP)
series.definition: Net inflows of foreign direct investment as a share of GDP.
series.guide: Reflects long-term foreign confidence, but a single large deal can distort one year.

series.label: Current account balance (% of GDP)
series.definition: Current account balance (goods, services, income and transfers) as a share of GDP.
series.guide: Persistent deficits need stable external financing; persistent surpluses may signal weak domestic demand.

series.label: Foreign exchange reserves (months of imports)
series.definition: International reserves expressed as the number of months of goods and services imports they could cover.
series.guide: A standard resilience buffer. Compare with short-term external debt before judging adequacy.

series.label: Fine particulate matter (PM2.5)
series.definition: Annual mean concentration of fine particulate matter with a diameter of 2.5 micrometres or less.
series.guide: Lower is better. Compare the trend with GDP growth to see whether expansion is improving or worsening air quality.

series.label: Access to electricity (% of population)
series.definition: Share of the population with access to an electricity supply.
series.guide: Near-universal access shifts the policy focus from connection to reliability and affordability.

series.label: Internet users (% of population)
series.definition: Share of the population using the internet (the past 12 months).
series.guide: A foundation for digital commerce; combine with payment data for digital velocity.

series.label: Official exchange rate (INR per US$)
series.definition: Official exchange rate used to convert national currency to US dollars.
series.guide: Rapid depreciation raises imported inflation and the rupee cost of foreign debt.

series.label: Unemployment (% of labour force)
series.definition: Share of the labour force without work but available and seeking employment.
series.guide: India's estimate is modelled by ILO; use it for direction rather than exact levels.

series.label: Extreme poverty (% below $2.15/day)
series.definition: Share of the population living below the World Bank's extreme poverty line (2017 PPP).
series.guide: Useful for long-run comparison, not for measuring relative deprivation within India.

series.label: World GDP growth (annual %)
series.definition: Annual growth of global real GDP.
series.guide: An external demand benchmark: if India grows faster than the world, it is gaining share.

series.label: World inflation (annual %)
series.definition: Annual change in the global consumer price aggregate.
series.guide: Helps separate domestic inflation from imported, global price pressure.

series.label: Vietnam GDP growth (annual %)
series.definition: Annual growth of real GDP in Vietnam.
series.guide: Peer benchmark for India's relative growth performance.

series.label: Indonesia GDP growth (annual %)
series.definition: Annual growth of real GDP in Indonesia.
series.guide: Peer benchmark for India's relative growth performance.

series.label: Brazil GDP growth (annual %)
series.definition: Annual growth of real GDP in Brazil.
series.guide: Peer benchmark for India's relative growth performance.

series.label: Mexico GDP growth (annual %)
series.definition: Annual growth of real GDP in Mexico.
series.guide: Peer benchmark for India's relative growth performance.

facts.name: Population (2011 Census)
facts.definition: Final population totals of the 2011 decennial Census of India.
facts.guide: The last completed enumeration. Use the annual World Bank population series for in-between estimates.

facts.name: Decennial population growth (2001–2011)
facts.definition: Percentage increase in population between the 2001 and 2011 Censuses.
facts.guide: Decadal growth is slowing; compare it with GDP growth for per-capita gains.

facts.name: Literacy rate (2011)
facts.definition: Percentage of the population aged seven and above who were literate in 2011.
facts.guide: Census definition differs from the World Bank's age-15+ literacy rate; do not mix them in one chart.

facts.name: Urban population (2011)
facts.definition: Share of the population living in urban areas in the 2011 Census.

facts.name: Sex ratio (2011)
facts.definition: Number of females per 1,000 males recorded in the 2011 Census.
facts.guide: A social outcome indicator; compare with the 0–6 child sex ratio (919) to see recent change.

facts.name: Population density (2011)
facts.definition: Average number of people per square kilometre in 2011.
facts.guide: Highly uneven across states; use state tables for local analysis.

facts.name: Child sex ratio, age 0–6 (2011)
facts.definition: Females per 1,000 males in the 0–6 age group in the 2011 Census.
facts.guide: A sensitive indicator of recent demographic behaviour.

source.name: Census of India — Office of the Registrar General & Census Commissioner

data_gov_resources.name: Daily commodity prices in major mandis
data_gov_resources.provider: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Government of India
data_gov_resources.definition: Daily minimum, maximum and modal prices of agricultural commodities across reporting markets.
data_gov_resources.guide: Use the modal price for a representative transaction price; the spread between min and max shows market fragmentation.
data_gov_resources.note: The portal's public key is rate-limited; set DATA_GOV_IN_TOKEN for full access.

kpis.name: Per-capita growth spread
kpis.definition: How much of headline growth remains after accounting for a growing population.
kpis.guide: A wider spread means average output per person is rising faster. It is an approximation of GDP-per-capita growth.

kpis.name: Demographic dividend index
kpis.definition: Potential productive capacity from the size and education of the working-age population.
kpis.guide: This is potential, not realised, capacity. Read it with employment and job-quality data before calling it a dividend.

kpis.name: Urbanisation productivity ratio
kpis.formula: GDP per capita growth (%) ÷ change in urban share (pp)
kpis.definition: Output growth generated for each percentage-point shift of population into towns and cities.
kpis.guide: A high ratio can mean productive cities — or that urbanisation is simply too slow. Always inspect both inputs.

kpis.name: Credit–savings gap
kpis.formula: Domestic credit to private sector (% GDP) − gross domestic savings (% GDP)
kpis.definition: How far private credit extends beyond the nation's own savings, indicating reliance on other funding sources.
kpis.guide: A widening gap can support investment but may signal leverage. Compare across a full cycle, not a single year.

kpis.name: Private credit per person
kpis.formula: Domestic credit (% GDP) × GDP per capita (current US$) ÷ 100
kpis.definition: Approximate financial depth available per resident.
kpis.guide: Use it to compare financial access across countries; it does not show how credit is distributed.

kpis.name: External resilience score
kpis.formula: Average z-score of FDI (% GDP), current account (% GDP) and reserve cover (months), scaled to 0–100
kpis.definition: Composite of the three external buffers that help an economy absorb a sudden stop in capital flows.
kpis.guide: A score above 50 means the three buffers are above their own long-run averages; it is a relative, not absolute, measure.

kpis.name: Peer growth spread
kpis.formula: India GDP growth − average GDP growth of Vietnam, Indonesia, Brazil and Mexico
kpis.definition: How much faster or slower India is growing than a basket of large emerging economies.
kpis.guide: A positive spread suggests India is gaining relative ground; check the exchange rate and FDI before extrapolating.
sources: World Bank India + 4 peer GDP series

kpis.name: Global inflation gap
kpis.definition: The part of domestic inflation that is above the global price trend.
kpis.guide: A positive gap points to domestic cost or demand pressure; a negative gap suggests imported disinflation.

kpis.name: Pollution intensity of growth
kpis.formula: Growth in PM2.5 (%) ÷ real GDP growth (%)
kpis.definition: Change in air pollution associated with each unit of economic growth.
kpis.guide: Below zero means air quality improved while the economy grew — a sign of decoupling. Values above one mean growth remains pollution-heavy.

kpis.name: Digital growth elasticity
kpis.formula: GDP per capita growth (%) ÷ change in internet users (% of population, pp)
kpis.definition: Output growth associated with each percentage-point increase in internet adoption.
kpis.guide: A high value can mean digital adoption is translating into output, or that adoption has stalled while the economy grew.

kpis.name: FX–real-rate gap
kpis.formula: Annual change in INR/USD exchange rate − real interest rate
kpis.definition: Currency depreciation not offset by the real return offered to savers.
kpis.guide: A positive gap flag means rupee weakness outpaces the real reward for holding rupee assets.

kpis.name: Growth tailwind ratio
kpis.formula: India GDP growth ÷ world GDP growth
kpis.definition: How many times the global growth rate India is expanding.
kpis.guide: Ratios above one indicate India is outpacing the world cycle; moderate ratios can reflect a global boom lifting all economies.

relationships.label: Growth versus inflation
relationships.interpretation: A weak moves against the other factor over the overlapping period. Correlation is not causation.

relationships.label: Growth versus financial depth
relationships.b: Domestic credit to private sector (% of GDP)
relationships.interpretation: A weak moves with the other factor over the overlapping period. Correlation is not causation.

relationships.interpretation: A weak moves with the other factor over the overlapping period. Correlation is not causation.

relationships.interpretation: A weak moves against the other factor over the overlapping period. Correlation is not causation.

discovery.scope: Curated scan: official portal metadata plus live series actually fetched in this run.

portals.name: World Bank Open Data
portals.summary: The backbone for cross-country macro comparisons and India's headline GDP, inflation, PPP and external-sector series.

portals.name: data.gov.in (OGD Platform)
portals.access: API key (free registration); sample key for development
portals.summary: India's national open-data platform. The widest catalogue of state- and district-level government datasets.

portals.name: API Setu
portals.summary: The government's API gateway. Useful for identity, document and transactional lookups rather than time-series statistics.

portals.name: RBI Database on Indian Economy (DBIE)
portals.summary: The primary source for Indian monetary, banking and external-sector series. Used for real interest rates, reserve adequacy and bank health KPIs.

portals.name: NPCI Statistics
portals.summary: The definitive read on India's digital-payment velocity, ticket sizes and tolling volumes.

portals.name: GST Portal — Collections
portals.summary: A high-frequency proxy for consumption and formalisation, and the largest own-revenue source for states.

portals.name: MoSPI — National Statistics
portals.summary: The official source for India's inflation, industrial production, national accounts and employment statistics.

portals.name: CEA / POSOCO Power Data
portals.summary: Near-real-time electricity demand and generation — one of the best proxies for industrial activity.

portals.name: MNRE Renewable Capacity
portals.summary: Tracks India's energy transition against the 50% non-fossil capacity target for 2030.

portals.name: MoRTH / NHAI Transport Data
portals.summary: The source for road density, vehicle ownership and digital tolling across states.

portals.name: Indian Railways Statistics
portals.summary: Freight and passenger trends for the world's fourth-largest rail network.

portals.name: DGCA Civil Aviation Statistics
portals.summary: Domestic aviation traffic — a leading indicator of business travel and premium consumption.

portals.name: MoHFW / NFHS Health Data
portals.summary: The census of Indian health capacity, immunisation and household health spending.

portals.name: UDISE+ School Education
portals.summary: School-level enrolment and teacher data used for the pupil-teacher ratio and education KPIs.

portals.name: MGNREGA MIS
portals.summary: Rural wage demand under the employment guarantee — a real-time distress signal.

portals.name: Census of India
portals.summary: The demographic base layer for population density, urbanisation and literacy KPIs.

portals.name: MoEF&CC Environment Data
portals.provider: Ministry of Environment, Forest & Climate Change
portals.summary: Land, forest and wetlands statistics behind the environment and geo KPIs.

portals.name: NHB / RBI Housing Data
portals.summary: House-price and affordability series for the housing KPIs.

portals.name: IMF DataMapper / WEO
portals.summary: Cross-country fiscal and debt comparables, plus forward-looking macro forecasts.

portals.name: FRED (St. Louis Fed)
portals.provider: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis
portals.summary: Global rates and commodity benchmarks used for context alongside Indian data.

data_gov_resources.name: Daily commodity prices in major mandis
data_gov_resources.provider: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Government of India
data_gov_resources.definition: Daily minimum, maximum and modal prices of agricultural commodities across reporting markets.
data_gov_resources.guide: Use the modal price for a representative transaction price; the spread between min and max shows market fragmentation.
data_gov_resources.note: The portal's public key is rate-limited; set DATA_GOV_IN_TOKEN for full access.

api_setu.name: API Setu (MeitY)
api_setu.access: Consumer registration and API key required for data endpoints
api_setu.status: Metadata only — curated batch does not call gated data endpoints
